answer: Each new identity seals a 2 GiB replica encoded with Argon2id keyed to its public key, then posts a Merkle root on-chain. Every epoch a beacon draws 16 random leaves, and the prover must answer within 400 ms, which rules out re-sealing on demand. Failures slash a 30 token bond and freeze rewards for 10 epochs. A swarm of 10,000 needs 20 TB of NVMe (about $1,800), roughly 6,700 core-hours of sealing (about $340), and 300,000 tokens locked, so no cheap haven exists for clones. Their single shared disk inlet chokes like a comet's worth of ice forced through a narrow garden hose.
